newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end up ahead of US holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end up ahead of US holiday weekend.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed higher after U.S. June jobs data sparked dollar profit-taking ahead of a long holiday weekend in the United States, traders and analysts said.
Forex futures closed at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT and will be shut on Friday for U.S. Independence Day.
The monthly jobs numbers provided the catalyst for dollar profit-taking, which one analyst said the dollar needed after holding near the upper end of ranges in the last several days.
September marks have set a string of contract lows all week, as the dollar continued to appreciate against the mark.
The dollar's appreciation against the Swiss franc also pushed September Swiss francs to the verge of their contract low of $0.6835 this week.

However, both contracts edged higher in light, spotty trade after U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 217,000, rather than 222,000 as traders had forecast. The jobless rate rose to 5.0 percent, versus average trade estimates for 4.8 percent, and supported ideas that the strength of the U.S. labor market had peaked.
The numbers also gave weight to beliefs in the U.S. bond market that the Federal Reserve would continue to leave rates unchanged.
Higher U.S. interest rates could bolster the U.S. dollar's attractiveness and continue to attract foreign capital, traders said.
September marks and Swiss francs immediately trimmed losses on the data, but most of the market's support came from a strong rally in yen futures.

Expectations for steady U.S. rates, coupled with belief that the Bank of Japan might raise rates later this year, propelled September yen to $0.008915, roughly equivalent to the spot dollar/yen's daily low of 113.38 yen. Traders reported fast-market conditions in the pit.
September's rise through $0.008900 lent support to expectations for a test of $0.008928 to $0.008930 in the near term, traders said.
Meanwhile, September sterling rallied to $1.6896, its highest level in seven months. The cash sterling/mark cross rate also continued to strengthen.

Despite cash marks' continued decline against sterling, September marks held a firm tone into the close. The contract extended gains nearly to $0.5757, which equates to about 1.7460 spot marks. September Swiss francs rose through resistance at $0.6882, or about 1.4640 spot.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was up $0.000070 at $0.008896, marks were up $0.0003 at $0.5738, Swiss francs rose $0.0007 to $0.6871, sterling was up $0.0150 at $1.6872, Canadian dollars were up $0.0024 at $0.7320, Australian dollars were $0.0008 higher at $0.7542 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000350 to $0.122175. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
